What is vegetative propagation?
questions.a: New plants growing from vegetative parts - root, stem or leaf - of the parent, without seeds or flowers.

questions.q: Name a plant that propagates by leaves and one by stems.
questions.a: Bryophyllum buds grow on leaf margins; potato (stem tuber) and rose stems propagate by stems.

questions.q: State one advantage and one disadvantage of vegetative propagation.
questions.a: Advantage: plants grow faster and stay true to type. Disadvantage: no variation, so diseases pass on and new traits don't arise.

concepts.title: Asexual Reproduction by Budding and Spore Formation

questions.q: How does yeast reproduce by budding?
questions.a: A bud grows out of the parent cell, the nucleus divides, and the bud pinches off as a new yeast cell.

questions.q: How does Rhizopus (bread mould) spread by spores?
questions.a: Sporangia burst to release thick-walled spores that float in air and germinate on moist bread.

questions.q: Why do spores have thick walls?
questions.a: Thick walls protect them from harsh conditions until they meet moisture and food.

concepts.title: Anatomy and Functions of Floral Organs

questions.q: Name the four whorls of a flower from outside in.
What are the male and female gamete-bearing parts of a flower?
questions.a: Stamen (anther makes pollen with male gametes) and carpel (ovule holds the egg).

questions.q: What happens inside the ovule after fertilisation?
questions.a: The zygote forms an embryo; the ovule matures into a seed with stored food and a protective coat.

concepts.title: Fertilisation and Reproductive Strategies in Animals

questions.q: What is external fertilisation? Give an example.
questions.a: Eggs and sperms meet outside the parents' bodies, as in frogs and most fish, in water.

questions.q: Why do animals with external fertilisation lay hundreds of eggs?
questions.a: Eggs and young are exposed to predators and water currents, so large numbers ensure some survive.

questions.q: How is internal fertilisation an advantage?
questions.a: The developing embryo is protected inside the mother's body, so fewer gametes are wasted.

questions.q: Name the male reproductive parts in humans.
questions.a: A pair of testes, sperm ducts (vas deferens), accessory glands and the penis.

questions.q: Name the female reproductive parts in humans.
questions.a: A pair of ovaries, oviducts (fallopian tubes), uterus and vagina.

questions.q: Where do sperms and eggs meet in the human body?
questions.a: In the oviduct (fallopian tube), where fertilisation occurs.

concepts.title: Contraception and Sexually Transmitted Infection Prevention

questions.q: How do condoms help reproductive health?
questions.a: They prevent pregnancy and also protect against sexually transmitted infections.

questions.q: Name two categories of contraceptive methods.
questions.a: Barrier methods (condom) and hormonal/surgical methods (pills, vasectomy, tubectomy, copper-T).

questions.q: Why is sex education important for adolescents?
questions.a: It corrects myths, prevents infections and early pregnancy, and promotes responsible behaviour.
